stories.title: Effect of dual rinse irrigation with activation techniques on dentinal tubule penetration of a bioceramic sealer: an in vitro confocal laser microscopy study
stories.description: Complete sealing of the apical canal anatomy enhances micromechanical interlocking, prevents microbial invasion, and contributes to the long-term success of endodontic treatment. This study evaluated the effect of dual rinse hydroxyethylidene diphosphonate (HEDP) irrigation on the dentinal tubule penetration of a bioceramic sealer compared with that of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) and chlorhexidine gluconate (CHX), with and without activation. One hundred mandibular premolars were prepared using ProTaper Ultimate and assigned to three irrigation protocols (n = 30) and a non-activated control group (n = 10). Irrigants were applied using manual dynamic activation (MDA) or sonic activation (EDDY), resulting in six subgroups (n = 15). After obturation with AH Plus Bioceramic Sealer, sections at 1–2 mm, 5–6 mm, and 9–10 mm from the apex were analyzed using confocal laser scanning microscopy. Maximum penetration depth (MPD), average penetration (AP), and penetration percentage (PP) were measured. Statistical analysis was performed in SPSS v24 using the Kruskal–Wallis and Friedman tests with Bonferroni correction (p < 0.05). In the apical third, EDTA–MDA showed significantly higher MPD and AP than HEDP–MDA. CHX–EDDY demonstrated higher PP than CHX-MDA. Overall, HEDP resulted in lower dentinal tubule penetration than EDTA, particularly apically. Irrigation protocol and activation technique significantly influenced sealer penetration behavior.

stories.title: Clinical motor coordination, postural control, and simple reaction speed following a 12-week Khon Kaen Qigong program in older adults with mild cognitive impairment: a controlled pre–post study
stories.description: This study examined whether a 12-week Khon Kaen Qigong (KKQ) program was associated with changes in clinical motor coordination, postural control, and simple reaction speed in older adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI). A prospective, parallel-group, controlled pre–post design was used. The manuscript-specific analysis included 62 older adults with MCI with 31 participants in the KKQ group and 31 in the usual-lifestyle control group. The KKQ group completed supervised training three times weekly, 60 min per session, for 12 weeks. The manuscript-specific primary outcomes were the study-recorded finger-to-nose, rapid alternating-movement, and gait/posture scores; mean ruler-drop reaction distance was the secondary outcome. Between-group differences in individual change scores were examined using two-sided Mann–Whitney U tests, with Holm adjustment across the three primary outcomes. Mean reaction distance was additionally analysed using a linear mixed-effects model, and the ordered clinical scores were examined using exploratory adjusted ordinal regression models. Complete baseline and week-12 records were available for all 62 participants included in the analysis. The KKQ group was older and had a higher baseline MoCA score than the control group. No statistically significant between-group differences were observed in changes in the three clinical coordination scores (Holm-adjusted P = 0.666, 0.666, and 0.503) or in mean ruler-drop reaction distance (P = 1.000). Adjustment for age, body mass index, years of education, and baseline outcome values did not materially change the findings, and additional adjustment for baseline MoCA did not materially alter the results. Standardized between-group effect estimates were small (Hedges’ g between − 0.31 and + 0.14), and all 95% confidence intervals included the null value. The 12-week KKQ program was not associated with statistically detectable improvements in the specific clinical motor coordination, postural-control, or ruler-drop reaction outcomes assessed in this sample. These findings should not be interpreted as evidence that KKQ is ineffective for other cognitive, physical, or functional outcomes. Because the study did not include neuroimaging or instrumented neurophysiological measures, no cerebellum-specific mechanism was tested. Trial registration Thai Clinical Trials Registry, TCTR20211228001.

stories.title: Environmental impact of copper smelting on surrounding areas: case study of Kankoyo Township
stories.description: The impact of copper smelting on an urban settlement in Mufulira District of the Copperbelt Province in Zambia was investigated. The settlement shares a boundary with a copper smelter that was commissioned in the early 1930s and has resulted in the negative impact on the soil and vegetation. The study examined the condition of both topsoil and subsoil layers to support the development of appropriate remediation strategies. A stratified, depth-resolved multivariate approach was used, with topsoil and subsoil analyzed separately to better understand their characteristics. The analysis considered the influence of pH, organic matter, elevation, distance from the copper smelter, and proximity to main roads on soil variability within each layer. The findings revealed that the soils were generally acidic, with organic matter levels below average. Copper concentrations were notably elevated, with mean values of 3780 mg/kg in the topsoil and 1400 mg/kg in the subsurface layer. Furthermore, distance from the smelter emerged as the dominant factor controlling PTE distribution, with Cu, Zn, and Pb concentrations decreasing with increasing distance, confirming the influence of smelter-derived deposition. Elemental patterns distinguished anthropogenic inputs (Cu, Zn, Pb) from geogenic controls (Fe, As). Soil pH and organic matter showed no systematic spatial trends but influenced local PTE retention and mobility. Two contrasting vertical behaviors were identified, with Fe, Cu, and Zn exhibiting strong inter-element associations and deeper soil integration, whereas Pb, Cd, and As showed limited downward migration, indicating differential post-depositional controls on PTE redistribution. Contamination indices revealed pronounced enrichment of Cu and Cd, moderate accumulation of Pb and Zn, and background levels of Fe, with surface soils acting as the primary reservoir of anthropogenic contamination and subsoils reflecting limited pollutant transport. Nonetheless, the amount of unexplained variation indicated that other environmental factors, or local-scale processes not captured in the present study, may also be contributing to the observed patterns. The analysed potentially toxic elements concentrations followed a decreasing order of Fe>Cu>Zn>Pb>Cd>As, with mercury undetectable from all sampled sites.
